opportunities.name: Research Studentships
eligibility_clues: The studentship supports full-time research students. Applicants are not required to apply separately. It is awarded on academic merit, subject to the academic department's decision, and indicated on the offer letter.
Part-time and self-funded students are not eligible.
Recipients need satisfactory academic progress and perform duties assigned by departments.
The admission comparison applies the same studentship line to the regular Research Postgraduate Programme (PhD and MPhil) and the ITS Transdisciplinary PhD Programme.
Department of Mathematics offers UGC-funded PhD and MPhil, year of entry 2027 September. Research areas on the programme page include scientific computing and optimisation.
The department CMS says offering of studentships is subject to the department's decision. That CMS block still labels an older year; the rate below is the Graduate School figure.
opportunities.amount_note: Fees page: 'For AY2026/27, the monthly studentship rate will be HK$19,310 (post-candidacy HK$19,660 for PhD).' The current-students page adds 'with effect from 1 September 2026'. No AY2027/28 studentship rate is printed on the Graduate School pages opened.
opportunities.deadline_note: No separate studentship deadline is printed. Regular PhD and MPhil applications for academic year 2027/28 open from 1 September 2026, with deadlines 1 December 2026 and 15 April 2027. The Mathematics programme page lists the same dates and a cut-off of 15 Apr 2027.
opportunities.match_rationale: This is the university monthly studentship for full-time PhD and MPhil students. Local students are not excluded, the Department of Mathematics programme covers computational mathematics, and the 2027/28 admission round is open. The printed monthly rate is labelled AY2026/27.
opportunities.intake_relevance: 2027/28 PhD and MPhil applications are open. The printed studentship rate is the AY2026/27 rate.
restrictions: Award is a departmental decision shown on the offer letter
Satisfactory academic progress and assigned departmental duties

opportunities.name: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme
eligibility_clues: HKBU invites candidates from all cultural and ethnic backgrounds for full-time PhD study under HKPFS.
Local applicants submit an HKID card. Non-local applicants submit a passport or other identity document.
Applicants for HKBU PhD programmes via HKPFS are concurrently considered for the regular postgraduate studentship.
The Department of Mathematics programme page invites HKPFS applications and lists scientific computing among its research areas.

HKPFS at a Glance (AY2027/28) also states tuition waived annually for 4 years, a conference and research-related travel allowance, and university-arranged shared-room accommodation in the first two years.
Subject to satisfactory academic progress.
opportunities.amount_note: HKPFS introduction, under HKPFS at a Glance (AY2027/28): 'HK$28,700 (approx. US$3,680) monthly' and 'HK$344,400 (approx. US$44,200) annually for 4 years'. The same glance lists the travel allowance as 'HK$14,400 (approx. US$1,850) per year for a maximum of 3 years' plus the University's Research Support Fund of HK$25,000 for the 4-year study period.
opportunities.deadline_note: The cited introduction page does not print the application deadline. The admission timeline page prints 1 Sep - 1 Dec 2026 (Hong Kong Time 12:00 noon) for the RGC step and 1 Sep - 1 Dec 2026 (Hong Kong Time 23:59) for the HKBU full application. Those phrases stay off this deadline field while source_url remains the introduction page.
opportunities.match_rationale: The AY2027/28 round pays a monthly stipend for full-time PhD study. Local applicants are included through the HKID requirement, and the Mathematics PhD page invites HKPFS applications in areas that include scientific computing. MPhil is outside this scheme.
opportunities.intake_relevance: AY2027/28. Applications run from 1 September 2026 to 1 December 2026.
restrictions: Initial application is made to the RGC, then a full application to HKBU quoting the HKPFS reference number
The University may review the types of incentives depending on funding and strategic planning

opportunities.name: Tuition Waiver for Local Research Postgraduate (RPg) Students
eligibility_clues: HKBU Graduate School: starting from 2018/19, the Government provides a tuition waiver for all local students enrolled in UGC-funded RPg programmes.
UGC page: non-means-tested waiver for local full-time students in UGC-funded RPg programmes at Hong Kong Baptist University and the other UGC-funded universities.
FAQ: UGC-funded RPg programmes mainly include all full-time MPhil and PhD programmes. Part-time RPg programmes are not funded by UGC.
Category I includes a person holding a Hong Kong permanent identity card. Category II, including non-local students, cannot qualify.

The eligibility revision applies to the 2027/28 academic year and thereafter. The FAQ sets a one-year transitional residency requirement for 2027/28 and two years from 2028/29 for the dependant-visa category.
Eligible local students need not apply. The university waives the tuition fees.
FAQ: an HKPFS stipend or other scholarship that does not aim to cover tuition fees leaves the waiver in place.
opportunities.amount_note: FAQ: 'The tuition fee for the above mentioned UGC-funded RPg programmes gradually increases from HK$42,100 in 2024/25 Academic Year (AY) to HK$44,500 in 2025/26 AY, HK$47,000 in 2026/27 AY and HK$49,500 in 2027/28 AY.' The scheme page states that the entire tuition fee of eligible students will be waived. HKBU's fees page lists the same UGC-funded full-time figures, $47,000 for 2026/27 and $49,500 for 2027/28. This is a fee waiver, not a living stipend.
opportunities.deadline_note: FAQ: 'The university will waive the tuition fees of eligible local students enrolled in the UGC-funded RPg programmes. They need not apply for the scheme.' No application deadline is printed.
opportunities.match_rationale: A local Hong Kong permanent resident in a full-time UGC-funded Mathematics PhD or MPhil is in the group whose tuition the scheme waives, and the FAQ prints the 2027/28 tuition fee. It is a tuition waiver alongside the studentship, rather than the monthly living stipend.
opportunities.intake_relevance: The revised eligibility applies to the 2027/28 academic year and thereafter. The application cycle for 2027/28 commences in October 2026.
restrictions: A student whose tuition is already fully waived by another scheme is not waived again under this scheme

opportunities.name: Global Research Fellowship Scheme
eligibility_clues: Supports eligible PhD students undertaking an in-person non-local research attachment or research internship at a designated institution for at least one month.
The student must be enrolled in a full-time PhD programme and be a studentship recipient with satisfactory academic progress.
Faculties and schools nominate within quotas. Retrospective nominations are not considered.
The admission table lists a maximum of HK$60,000 for HKPFS, regular PhD students, and the ITS pathway, by faculty or school nomination.
opportunities.amount_note: Research Support Fund page: 'Up to HK$60,000 per student.' Funding covers basic economy-class return airfare and a subsistence allowance, normally on a 2:1 matching basis. Each student may receive support for one attachment or internship only.
opportunities.deadline_note: Students contact their Faculty or School for nomination details. No calendar deadline is printed. The attachment should be completed during the normal study period and normally no later than the end of the academic year following the application year.
opportunities.match_rationale: A full-time Mathematics PhD student who holds the studentship can be nominated for this attachment fellowship, including a local student. It funds one overseas attachment rather than the monthly living stipend, and MPhil students are outside the eligibility list.
opportunities.intake_relevance: For enrolled full-time PhD studentship recipients during the normal study period. No 2027/28 nomination date is printed.
restrictions: Faculty or school nomination and quota
One attachment or internship per student
In-person duration of at least one month

opportunities.name: Research Support Fund
eligibility_clues: Full-time PhD or MPhil students receiving a full studentship during their normal study period may apply for reimbursement.

opportunities.match_rationale: A local full-time Mathematics PhD or MPhil student who receives the full studentship can claim this research-expense fund. It reimburses conference and related costs up to a capped total, rather than paying the monthly living stipend.
opportunities.intake_relevance: The printed entitlement applies to newly admitted studentship recipients from the 2026/27 cohort onwards. No separate 2027/28 cap is printed.

blockers: WebFetch of https://www.math.hkbu.edu.hk/programmes/rpg returned an empty JavaScript shell. The department text used here was read from the published CMS at https://cms.math.hkbu.edu.hk/api/webpage-contents, which the fees route https://www.math.hkbu.edu.hk/programmes/rpg/admission/application-fee loads. That CMS studentship block, updated in 2024, still prints a 2024/25 monthly stipend of HK$18,550 (HK$19,070 after PhD candidacy) and UGC tuition of HK$42,100. Those older figures were not used as the current studentship. The Graduate School fees page prints the AY2026/27 rate and does not print an AY2027/28 studentship rate.

The Computer Science HKPFS awardee scholarship is 'up to HK$15,000 per month' on the Office of Student Affairs list and 'Up to HK$22,000 per month for a maximum of four years' on the faculty PDF last updated 11 August 2026. The opportunity keeps the Student Affairs figure. The PDF figure was not substituted.

The faculty PDF prints HK$10,000 for the Yakun scheme limited to Faculty of Science mainland research postgraduates. The Office of Student Affairs row prints 'no fixed amount' for Chinese Mainland students. The Yakun opportunity uses the Student Affairs phrase.

Every Author First Publication Scholarship and the university Outstanding PhD Thesis Award are named on the Graduate School fees page. No opened page printed an amount, a deadline, or full eligibility rules for those two university awards.

The Office of Student Affairs postgraduate table also lists many taught-programme and other-faculty awards in Business, Communication, Chinese Medicine, Creative Arts, Translation, History, Social Work, and Education. Those rows were read. Separate opportunities were written for university-wide research awards, Mathematics, Computer Science, Physics, taught mathematical programmes, and the clearest non-local or taught schemes. The remaining taught awards on that page are not each repeated.
Search results pointed to an AY2026/27 leaflet at https://gs.hkbu.edu.hk/f/page/1313/RPg%20Leaflet%20(AY2627)_for_website.pdf. That PDF was not opened, and its figures were not used.
